question: Road freight transport associations in nine Member States have called for an ambitious agreement on the revision of the Weights and Dimensions Directive. In order to achieve the green transition, the industry needs a pragmatic legislative framework that will offer road hauliers tangible incentives to invest.

To promote the roll-out of zero-emission vehicles, there must be adequate weight compensation for using clean technologies. The solutions adopted must not lead to a reduction in payloads or the overloading of driving axles compared to conventional diesel lorries. This will help guarantee the financial viability of electric fleets. Furthermore, operational efficiency requires flexibility.

It is essential to facilitate highcapacity freight between neighbouring Member States that share the same rules, in particular by promoting European Modular Systems (EMS) and allowing 44-tonne lorries to cross borders where domestic regulations permit. This would effectively reduce energy consumption, emissions and the number of lorries on the road.
How will the Commission support these priorities in order to reconcile its Green Deal objectives with economic realities and the operational flexibility that EU road hauliers need?
